newsitem.title: USA: N.J. reviews Monroe's bond-financed school - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. reviews Monroe's bond-financed school - paper.

text.p: New Jersey officials are reviewing cost overruns on a $31 million bond-financed high school in Monroe, a project also at the center of a lawsuit by contractors, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.

Construction of the Williamstown High School is a year behind schedule, and state officials are reviewing documents to determine whether local officials improperly used general funds to cover cost overruns instead of bond proceeds, the newspaper said.
New Jersey officials are still deciding whether to begin a full-scale audit of the district.
Voters approved the high school construction plan in a 1993 bond referendum seeking $31 million. But local officials soon determined that the price would exceed that amount, the newspaper said.

Adding to the project's problems is a $3.5 million lawsuit filed by the former general contractor, William Hughes General Contractors Inc. The suit alleges the district failed to pay him nearly $1.3 million for finished work and was unable to prove it had enough money to finish construction.
